articleTitle: 2019 11th Asia-Pacific International Conference on Lightning (APL)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: lightning protection; lightning; earthing; arresters; poles and towers; power overhead lines; wind turbines; clouds; power distribution lines; overvoltage protection.

articleTitle: Measurements and calculations of rail potential in D. C. traction power supply system
abstract: In D.C. traction power supply system, high resistance grounding fault is one of the difficult problems for reliable power supply. Because the load current of trains is much higher than the grounding fault current, it is impossible to detect the fault from the over-current relay. The detection of three phase unbalance which is conventionally applied in A.C. power supply system is not applicable in D.C. traction power supply system, neither. Considering such a peculiarity of D.C. traction power supply, grounding fault detection based on the potential difference between rails and grounding mesh at traction substation is practically used for grounding fault detection at D.C. substation for railway in Japan. The rails of D.C. railway are electrically floating, not grounded intentionally, to avoid stray current caused by D.C. traction loads. Also, the rails are part of a D.C. traction power supply system, and can be an approach path for lightning to the substation. Studying the characteristics of the rail potential and the leakage current to the ground is also important for knowing the tendency of electricity when lightning current flows. In this study, the details of the behaviors of rail potential in urban D.C. railway system are investigated not only by the measurements in practical fields, but also by the calculations of D.C. traction power supply circuit. According to the previous experiences during a few decades, the rail potential near traction substation tends to be negative while it is positive at the location of train because of the voltage drop caused by the current in rails. Our measurement of rail potentials in Tokyo urban area, however, indicated that the rail potentials became positive in many cases. This result contradicts to the common sense of railway power supply engineers. We carried out circuit simulations for many cases and it was found that the rail potential tends to be positive in the traction power supply circuit with many trains. As conclusions, the rail potential becomes positive in the area where train operation density is high while it becomes negative where that is low. In addition, it was confirmed that two factors influence the fluctuation of the rail potential by continuous measurement of the rail potential. First, as the output current of the substation increases, the current leaking from the feeder circuit to the ground increases and the rail potential becomes negative. Second, the rail leakage resistance decreases due to rain, the leakage current increases and the rail potential becomes negative. In this paper, the details of our measurements and calculations will be shown.

articleTitle: Lightning Surge on the DC and AC Side of Solar PV System
abstract: The solar PV has become an alternative solution in Malaysia to generate electricity. Unfortunately the solar PV installed in Malaysia is attracted to the lightning strike. There were two points that have high possibilities of being strike by the lightning; on the DC side between the solar PV and inverter and on the AC side, between the inverter and the substation. Therefore, this study was performed to analyse the effects of lightning strike at these two different points at the solar PV farm without any lightning protection system (LPS).

articleTitle: Multi-Chamber Disc-Type Lightning Arrester for 13.8 kV Overhead Lines Protection
abstract: The article describes a multi-chamber disk-type arrester designed for lightning protection of 13.8 kV overhead lines, widely distributed in the countries of North and South America and South-East Asia. The simplicity and reliability of the design allows the arrester to withstand multiple impacts of direct lightning strikes without destruction. The conducted complex of electrical tests confirms the compliance of the arrester with international standards, and also proves the ability of the arrester to work in networks with short-circuit currents up to 26 kA.

articleTitle: Effect of group grounding on the potential rise across solar PV panels during lightning strike
abstract: Grounding systems play a vital role for dissipating the energy originating from a lightning stroke to the earth, functioning as an important component for protection and safety. In a solar photovoltaic (PV) farm, solar PV panels are fixed on a grounded structure with bolts and nuts. The structure, the frame of the PV panels, and the bolts and nuts are metallic (together called the assembly) and the layout of all assemblies of the entire solar farm depends on the terrain where they are installed. Lightning protection systems which are installed on a solar PV farm are mostly based on a Franklin rod (connected to a down-conductor) as the preferred point of attachment. These lightning rods can be installed either as isolated systems or as non-isolated systems from the solar panel assemblies. This paper is focused on the effect of group grounding on the potential rise across the solar PV panels during lightning strike. This whole assembly is simulated for various lightning attachment points in PSPICE using the lossy transmission line model. Voltage drop at various points in the assembly is measured for various soil resistivity. Based on the simulation results, group grounding of solar PV panels with middle grounding shows relatively low voltage drops compared to end grounding.

articleTitle: Statistical Lightning Study for 33kV Overhead Line in Peninsular Malaysia
abstract: This paper presents a statistical lightning study for 33kV overhead distribution line located in Northern area of Peninsular Malaysia during a period from 2008 to 2018. Data was collected by Lightning Detection System Network operated by TNB Research Sdn Bhd. The ground flash density and mean peak current maps of the selected line is produced. In addition, a cumulative probability distribution curve is obtained and compared to the widely used CIGRE curve. These few statistical parameters are useful in for several other applications, especially in determining the correct rating for arrester and in evaluating the performance of the line.

articleTitle: High voltage gradient zinc oxide varistors for line surge arresters and GIS tank-type arresters
abstract: In this work, we studied multiple dopants based ZnO varistors and optimizing its microstructure and electrical properties by tailoring the sintering characteristics. The properties were evaluated by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), current-voltage characteristics, capacitance-voltage characteristics, dielectric characteristics and X-ray diffraction characteristics. At a given gallium and indium concentration, the residual voltage ratio of the sintered varistors under the 5/20μs impulse current decreased obviously as the sintering temperature increased from 1100°C to 1250°C. Besides, the nonlinear coefficient was first increased and then decreased with increasing sintering temperature. The multiple doped ZnO varistors sintered at 1250°C showed optimal performance, exhibiting a grain size of 7.1μm, residual voltage ratio of 1.56, voltage gradient of 416 V/mm, leakage current of 0.79 μA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and nonlinear coefficient of 73. When applied in power systems, the high voltage gradient varistors will make the line surge arrester in better coordination with insulators as well as reach the goal of low cost and miniaturization of GIS tank-type arresters.

articleTitle: A Convolutional Neural Network for Classification of Lightning LF/VLF Waveform
abstract: With the accumulation of raw lightning data in various fields, it's more important to automatically analyze the large amounts of natural lightning data. In recent years, the neural network has made great process in pattern recognition, which makes it possible to efficiently classify the raw lightning data. In this study, a convolutional neural network is proposed for classification of lightning waveform in Low Frequency/ Very Low Frequency (LF/VLF) bands. The network is trained by a six-year (2012–2017) data set including over 50,000 lightning waveforms. By using a series of one-dimensional convolutions layer with rectified linear unit (ReLU) as its activation function, we use the labeled lightning time series directly as the input and train the network to get the classifier. The output of the network is a vector containing the results that an event belongs to each lightning type. We classify the types of lightning into five categories, including the cloud-to-ground (N/PCG) flash, ordinary intracloud (IC) flash, preliminary breakdown pulse (PB), narrow bipolar event (NBE) and the classifier has an average accuracy more than 95%. Furthermore, we apply the classifier to five isolated thunderstorm and give the actual accuracy of the NCG by manual checking.

articleTitle: Earth Networks Lightning Network and Dangerous Thunderstorm Alerts
abstract: The Earth Networks Total Lightning Network (ENTLN) incorporates advanced lightning location technology delivering competitive lightning detection efficiency and location accuracy. ENTLN can detect both in-cloud (IC) and cloud-to-ground (CG) lightning. It consists of over 1600 wideband sensors deployed in 40+ countries to detect lightning and generate faster-localized storm alerts. Since its initial deployment, several improvements were made over the years to enhance its performance and usability. Notable ones are the addition of many new sensors each year to improve detection efficiency and extend lightning detection coverage to any regions of the world. Firmware improvements have also been made to further increase sensitivity, and the implementation of a multi-parameter classification algorithm allows IC and CG pulses to be distinguished with very good accuracy. A performance study was conducted to evaluate the characteristics of the ENTLN. The results of the study show that the detection efficiency and the classification accuracy of the new ENTLN processor have greatly improved. ENTLN data is used to track the properties of storms cells, such as the lightning flash rate, cell direction, and speed as a basis for issuing alerts for thunderstorms that have the potential for severe weather. Most severe convective storms can generate high IC flash rate and high IC/CG flash-rate ratios. When rates exceed critical thresholds, Dangerous Thunderstorm Alerts (DTAs) are issued. The system helps in predicting the storm dangers by generating a DTA with significant lead time before the ground-level severe weather. Through the life of the DTA warned storm, the storm cells are monitored continuously, which enhances the situational awareness. In this study, we analyze several severe weather events to estimate the effectiveness of DTAs as well as implications for improving public safety.

articleTitle: Implementation and Use of Multi Chamber Arresters for 33kV Overhead Lines in Malaysia
abstract: Multi chambers arresters were installed on 33kV bare overhead line in Malaysia to improve the line trippings due to lightning. In this pilot study, the line was equipped with line fault indicators and auto recloser for transient event recording. Field monitoring was carried out to determine feasibility and reliability of the device in preventing line trippings due to lightning. The case study line has been experiencing a significant amount of lightning activities, a total of 1,805 lightning strikes, detected by TNBR Lightning Detection System during 6 months monitoring period with an average peak current of 18.61 kA. Observation of one-time indicators has shown that 31 out of 180 devices have operated during the monitoring period. Line lightning performance analysis was carried out to quantify the effectiveness of the device in reducing tripping rate.

articleTitle: The Influence of the Metal Mesh to the Attachment Manner of CFRP Wind Turbine Blades
abstract: Wind turbine blade with carbon fiber reinforced plastics (CFRP) beam has much better mechanism performance. However, it faces the severe problem of lightning protection due to the conductivity of CFRP. Metal mesh are installed on CFRP blades by many manufacturers in order to protect the main beam. The performance of the metal mesh was not fully tested with real blade tip. In this paper, the blade tip equipped with tip receptor and fully covered mesh are tested under both negative and positive switching impulses. The results show that the mesh has little influence on the attachment manner. The results between none-mesh GFRP and with-mesh CFRP blade is also compared.

articleTitle: Analysis of Surge Arrester Damage Accident on Distribution Line due to Winter Lightning
abstract: In recent years, surge arrester damage on the distribution line has been drawn attention. The authors analyzed surge arrester damage accidents that actually occurred in the Japanese winter lightning area by simulation and inferred the characteristics of the lightning current that caused the damage.

articleTitle: Lightning Impulse Strength of 275 kV and 132 kV Tower with Composite Crossarm
abstract: Severe lightning overvoltage is regarded to the multiple flashovers on the overhead lines. Therefore, it signifies the needs of having a robust insulation system, especially to those which highly susceptible to lightning strikes. In order to minimize the impact of lightning, it is necessary to evaluate lightning performance of the tower and its components before implementing any proposed design. Therefore, in this work, a feasibility study was done on proposed 275 kV and 132 kV transmission tower with composite crossarm installed. In order to assess the insulation strength of the tower against the lightning activities, lightning caused events i.e. backflashover and shielding failure were applied onto the tower models by using FEM based software. The CFO of the tower insulation were calculated based on the design provided, whereby it was complementary verified by the voltage and electric field profiles of the simulation. For each case, none had shown a voltage magnitude higher than the voltage supposed to possibly cause 50% chance of flashover.

articleTitle: Cloud-to-Ground Lightning Activity in Guangdong Province, South China During the Period 2004–2017
abstract: Cloud-to-Ground (CG) lightning in Guangdong Province, South China has been observed over decades by the Lightning Location System (LLS) operated by power sector in China. In this paper, we present the characteristics of CG lightning based on the data collected during 2004-2017 when the LLS performance was relatively steady from year to year. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first time to investigate CG lightning from such a long period in this area. Over 30 (67) million CG lightning flashes (strokes) were recorded during this 14-year period. Various characteristics, including flash density, peak current, multiplicity, ratio of positive CG lightning, lightning day, etc, are investigated. Interesting spatiotemporal patterns of the CG lightning parameters are obtained and the potential causes are discussed.

articleTitle: Electric Field Distribution on Surface of Metamaterial under Lightning Impulse
abstract: In the aircrafts, metamaterials, by virtue of the special performance, have been widely used in the radome area, which is also the possible initial lightning attachment place during flight in thunderstorm days. In order to study the lightning attachment behavior of metamaterial, we analyze the electric field intensity distribution of the metamaterial plate in the vicinity of a lightning leader, and for the sake of comparison, similar analyses are also conducted to the insulated plate. It is found that there is a significant difference in electrical properties between metamaterials and insulated materials. Moreover, after arranging the antenna below the plates, the lightning is more likely to attach to the surface of the metamaterial than to the insulated plate. Furthermore, it appears that the lightning diverter strips, which are used to divert the lightning current to ground of aircraft, has better protection effect for the insulated materials than for the metamaterial one. Obtained results can provide a guiding significance to the application of metamaterial in regard of its lightning protection.

articleTitle: Influence of Grounding Design around Down Lead on Lightning Impulse Behavior of Substation Grounding Grid
abstract: The lightning impulse behavior of substation grounding grids plays a very important role in lightning protection of substations and the grounding design of the grounding grid around the down leads has great influence on it. This paper analyzed the lightning impulse behavior of substation grounding grids with different grounding designs around the down lead, including the connection points, local refinement and layout of vertical grounding poles around down leads. Results showed that special designs around down leads including multi-point connection, local refinement and vertical grounding poles could improve the transient behavior of substation grounding grid. Meanwhile only increasing the number of vertical grounding poles cannot improve the transient behavior significantly.

articleTitle: Smart IoT Monitoring System for Surge Protective Devices (SPDs)
abstract: A smart monitoring system with internet connectivity opens up the possibility to bring surge protective devices (SPDs) into the internet of things (IoT). Each voltage or current impulse at the SPD is measured and the measurement data is transferred into a cloud based storage. The cloud frontend opens many options to analyze the measured data and to derive the actual status of the SPD. By assessment of the impact of all stress events the pre-damages of the arrester can be determined to evaluate its actual “State of Health” (SoH). Even an estimation of the residual lifetime becomes feasible. With all this collected information maintenance requirements become predictable and maintenance work can be planned much more efficiently.

articleTitle: Lightning Protection of 110 kV and 220 kV Transformer Neutral Points in Shenzhen Power Grid
abstract: At present, the neutral point of ungrounded transformer in our country is usually protected by gap and/or arrester. The overvoltage including lightning overvoltage and power frequency overvoltage may cause misoperation of protection gap or thermal collapse of arrester, which affects the safe and reliable operation of the system. In recent years, Shenzhen power grid has suffered several faults caused by inappropriate neutral point protection measures or unreasonable parameter configuration of 110kV and 220kV transformers. Therefore, this paper explored two solutions. (1) One is a new lightning protection measure for transformer neutral point. This measure is combined with controllable clearance and metal oxide arrester (MOA). Under lightning overvoltage, the arrester operates. Under power frequency overvoltage, the gap breaks down to protect transformer neutral point insulation and arrester. Such measure can effectively solve the following problems. The arrester is prone to explosion when it operates under power frequency overvoltage. The clearance cannot extinguish arc when it operates under lightning and power frequency overvoltage impulse. The insulation coordination between the clearance and the parallel protection of the arrester is difficult. (2) A new type of relay protection configuration is adopted to avoid possible malfunction of system protection. The above two measures can greatly improve the stability and security of the system, and at the same time, vigorously enhance the level of intelligence of 110 and 220 kV substations, effectively promote the construction of intelligent substations. In the future, more simulation and experimental verification works for the above two measures will be carried out.

articleTitle: Analysis of Lightning Overvoltage According to Position of Lightning-Induced Voltage at the Solar Power Plant
abstract: In this paper, the lightning overvoltages are analyzed and compared in two specific situations: lightning applied directly to the PV array, and lightning that occurs at a point away from the PV array. The position of the lightning strike point is also considered to determine the influence of the distance between the strike point and PV array on lightning overvoltage. Lightning overvoltage causes serious damage to facilities in a solar power plant. To solve this problem, the characteristics of the overvoltage must be analyzed precisely. The information on lightning overvoltage generated by direct strike and lightning strikes at three different locations is discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Calculation of Wire Breaking Rate of Medium-Voltage Distribution Line due to Lightning
abstract: Lightning outage rate calculation is important to implement effective lightning countermeasures for medium voltage distribution lines, therefore, many studies of flashover calculation due to indirect and direct lightning strokes have been carried out. In these studies, flashover is regarded as an outage. On the other hand, observation results have suggested that flashover does not necessarily lead to lightning failure. In this paper, we proposed a procedure for calculating the rate of wire breaking of medium-voltage distribution lines considering arc melting characteristics of insulate wire and estimated the wire breaking rates of model distribution lines.

articleTitle: A Method to Model Soil Structure Based on the Randomness and Fractality of Soil Pore
abstract: Recently, extensive researches had been carried out on soil impedance characteristic under lighting impulse current, and obtained some variation laws on soil impedance. For applying fractal theory to study soil electrical conductivity, this paper proposed a method to simulate soil structure based on its randomness and fractality. Considering soil structure irregularity, a certain randomness were introduced to both iteration graphics and process when establishing Random Pore Fractal(RPF) model. Initial Dimension, Iterations, Parameter Controlling the Disorderliness of Iterative Unit(PDIU) and Parameter for Gathering Pore(PGP) were important parameters to control the conformity between real soil structure and its model, of which the Initial Dimension and Iterations were determined by the maximum particle size, the PDIU and PGP were adjusted according to the characteristics of porosity and pore distribution. RPF model could be used to build a more realistic soil structure model, and could be applied to the study of soil micro-conductivity, which had a certain engineering significance in fractal studies relevant to Soil Physics.

articleTitle: Waveform Analysis of Lightning Induced Overvoltages on 10 kV Distribution Lines
abstract: Lightning induced overvoltage is an important cause of fault in distribution network, and it is also the culprit of electrical equipment damage. The former research mode about overvoltage of distribution lines is mainly using shrinkage model or simulation calculation, and lack of measured results as evidence. The On-line overvoltage monitoring system was used to monitor phase conductor overvoltage of distribution lines, including lightning overvoltage, internal overvoltage and electromagnetic transient on 10 kV distribution line in Foshan, the system recorded 61 lightning overvoltage records in 2016 on the 10kV Maning Line, and the number of return strokes was up to 17 times. The average positive peak value is about 5 kV, while the negative peak value is slightly smaller than the positive peak value. Whether positive or negative, the overvoltage amplitude of phase B is always the lowest and that of phase A is always the highest. The average 10%-90% rise time is about 5 μs and the average duration time is about 10 μs. The peak value of measured induced overvoltage is much lower than that calculated by the Rusck's model.

articleTitle: Study on Short-Circuit Current Performance of ±500kV DC Transmission Line Surge Arrester
abstract: In order to study the pressure release capability of ±500 kV DC transmission line surge arrester after short-circuit fault, ±500 kV Yichang-Shanghai line was taken as the engineering background to calculate the short-circuit current that may occur in the whole line. The surge arrester short-circuit current test device was built. At the same time, pressure release structure and mechanical performance of surge arrester were analyzed. Finally, the high and low short-circuit current performance tests were carried out. The results show that the maximum and minimum short-circuit currents along the ±500 kV DC transmission line are about 18 kA and 5 kA. According to the short-circuit current series specified in IEC 60099-4, the surge arrester needs to withstand short-circuit currents are 50 kA and 800 A, respectively. The designed pressure release structure with a waist groove type can release the short-circuit fault energy effectively. It is verified that the short-circuit current performance of the surge arrester can meet the technical requirements of ±500 kV DC transmission project.

articleTitle: Research on Lightning Activity at High Altitude in Tibet
abstract: Tibet is in the southwest of Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, which owns expansive territory. As the transmission line between Tibet and Sichuan has been connected, the total number of important power transmission channel become larger, and lightning trip-out faults are more serious. Average altitude of Tibet is above 4000m, which cause different lightning activity in China. According to researching lightning Activity characteristic in Tibet, the basic lightning parameters can be got, which is very important for the designing and maintenance of the important transmission line. This passage count the lightning activity in Tibet from 2014 ~ 2018 year: firstly, by contrasting the total number of ground flash in each year, the strongest lightning activity happened in 2013 year, which is 0.229 times/(km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>·a); Secondly, by contrasting the difference of lightning in different area, the strongest lightning Activity happened in Lhasa and Shan-nan; Thirdly, by researching the cumulative probability distribution of lightning current amplitude, the middle lightning current is about 29kA; At last, the lightning density distributing graph of 500kV transmission lines in Tibet were analysed, the higher area were Qusum county, Gyaca county, Chagyab county and Markam county.

Author Keywords: cumulative probability distribution of lightning current amplitude

articleTitle: Research and Protection of Overvoltage Caused by Lightning Stroke on Wind Farm Collector Lines
abstract: Wind farms are usually built in the areas with frequent lightning activities. So their collector lines are vulnerable to lightning strikes, which threaten the safe operation of wind turbines and their supporting equipment. Based on the electromagnetic transient program ATP-EMTP, the lightning current model, the tower model, the collector line model, the insulator model and the arrester model were established, which were used to simulate lightning striking at the tower of collector lines. The influence on the line overvoltage was studied and the corresponding protective measures were discussed. The results show that the position of tower struck by lightning and the grounding resistance of the tower are the key factors affecting the overvoltage of the collector lines. For wind turbines at mountainous area, the lighting-induced overvoltage can be suppressed by reducing the grounding resistance of towers near the wind turbine and installing arresters at the tower nears wind turbine.

articleTitle: Application of insulation technology in tower lightning current measurement
abstract: Tower triggered lightning observation is one of the most important ways to measure lightning current waveforms. Scientists in many countries have built the lightning current measurements on high towers or high buildings lightning observations, their work form the cornerstone of lightning protection and natural lightning research. Measuring the natural lightning current is a difficult and important task. To measure more accurate waveforms, especially the continuous current characteristics of lightning, a wider bandwidth coaxial resistive shunt is preferred. With the shunt installed, the lightning rod must be sufficiently insulated from the tower frame before the connection to the coaxial resistive shunt. To ensure the safety of equipment and the reliability of measured data, power insulation is necessary. The following measurement results show that there has obvious interference in the current measurement results without insulation measures. After the insulation measures are taken, the interference does not exist.

articleTitle: Observation on Upward Lightning Induced by Nearby Positive Cloud-to-Ground Lightning based on Highspeed Camera and Radio Frequency Mapping System
abstract: Several lightning flashes observed on 325 m meteorological tower in Beijing, China. A high-speed video camera focused on the tower and four normal speed cameras focused on different directions that cover nearby high structures, the location of the towers is within the range of Beijing lightning network. In some thunderstorm, few of the positive lightning or intra-cloud flashes are initiating upward lightning from the towers. This work shows the features of the upward lightning due to these types of positive cloud to ground lightning near to towers. For this purposes, we have used highspeed video camera, normal speed camera, and radio frequency mapping data from Beijing Lightning NETwork (BLNET). BLNET, operated in Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei urban cluster area, has 16 stations and locates electromagnetic pulses radiated from cloud to ground and intra-cloud lighting. In nine of the analyzed flashes, two were simultaneously initiated upward lightning from different tower caused by same positive cloud to ground flash. Seven upward leaders were from single tower in which two of them were branched and in one case, the surface electric field was 3.5 kV/ m prior to the positive return stroke. In four cases, the upward leaders were associated with return stroke. Further, we considered tower lightning flash to validate our three-dimensional mapping of the flash and in the last a positive lightning three-dimensional development showed which initiated an upward leader.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of ACSR and ACCC Conductors on Corona Effect for Lightning Surge Studies
abstract: Corona effect plays an important role in determining the distortion and attenuation of the surges travelling along overhead transmission lines and thus could possibly cause the backflashover. This this paper presents a comparative analysis between the two conductors used for 275 kV transmission line in term of corona effect when subjected to the lightning surge propagation studies. The two conductors are the Aluminium Conductor Steel Reinforced (ACSR) and the new High-Temperature Low Sag (HTLS) conductor, known as Aluminium Conductor Composite Core (ACCC). Simulation using section by section method for a single conductor were simulated using PSCAD/EMTDC software. The analyses were done by comparing the results with three parameters that known to be affected the corona, namely the different conductor radius, the heights of the conductor above ground level, and the segment length used for a single conductor. The finding that can be drawn from the study is that the presence of ACCC conductor are found to be more efficient in reducing the corona effect than the ACSR conductors apart from other advantages such as higher current capacity and lesser losses as compared to ACSR.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Absorption Energy of Surge Arrester on Medium-Voltage Lines by Lightning to Wind Turbine in Winter
abstract: In recent years, the rate of burnout accidents due to excess energy capacity of surge arresters on medium-voltage distribution lines is increasing in lightning accidents. The upward lightning current from wind turbine in winter consists of ICC (Initial Continuous Current) and pulses superposing on it, and in many cases ICC dominates the measured charge amount. The authors calculate absorption energy of surge arresters on medium-voltage lines by the lightning strokes to the wind turbine in winter. From the calculated results, the authors show the influence of overhead ground wires, V-I characteristics of surge arresters and modeling method of lightning current waveforms.

articleTitle: Study on Direct Lightning Protection of $\pm\ 1100\text{kV}$ Converter Station Grid
abstract: The voltage level of HVDC transmission system in China has been raised from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 500\ kV$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 800\ kV$</tex> and further to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 1100\ kV$</tex> The transmission power has been raised from 3000MW to 12000 MW. It is the highest voltage level and transmission power in the world. It puts forward higher requirements for system stability, insulation coordination, layout of converter stations and equipment performance. Converter station is key of the DC power system. Once a lightning damage accident occurs, it may cause a large area blackout, and the impact is very serious. The converter station requires reliable lightning protection measurements. DC valve hall and indoor DC field of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm\ 1100\ kV$</tex> are higher than those of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 800\ kV$</tex> After height increase, the station lightning protection rod and line network could not effectively protect them. It was need to make lightning protection design alone for the valve hall and indoor DC field. In this paper, the design basis and design method of lightning protection for converter station buildings were given. By this method, the lightning protection design of valve hall and indoor DC field of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm\ 1100\ kV$</tex> Changji and Guquan converter station were checked and optimized. The research results have important reference value and guiding significance for lightning protection design of buildings in DC converter station and AC substation. With the operation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 1100\ kV$</tex> Changji-Guquan Project in 2019, the results of above research results will be gradually confirmed.

articleTitle: Application of Genetic Algorithm to Detect Disconnected Locations of Down Conductors along Wind Turbine Blades
abstract: This paper aims to present an approach based on genetic algorithm to obtain the most accurate location of the disconnected location of a down conductor along a wind turbine blade. The disconnected location is estimated from the simulation results carried out using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) model. The computed results of dipole antenna models are calculated by a numerical technique based on trapezoidal rule integration. To evaluate the performances of the proposed techniques, the calculated dipole antenna model is verified by comparing the FDTD simulation results. The comparison of the simulation results and estimated results showed that the proposed techniques exhibit good performance in the detection of disconnected locations.

articleTitle: Study on Distribution Characteristics of Leakage Current in DC Field of Converter Station
abstract: The corrosion condition of the grounding grid of the converter station is very important to ensure the safety and stability of the power system. From the perspective of the leakage current of the converter station equipment, the circuit model of the leakage current in the DC field of the converter station is proposed; According to the leakage current characteristics, the DC field of the converter station is divided into the high-voltage side and the neutral-pole side area; According to the actual situation of the converter station, a measurement and analysis platform suitable for the leakage current of the converter station equipment is built; Through field test, the leakage current of each area equipment is measured and analyzed, and the distribution characteristics of equipment leakage current in different areas are summarized; According to the measurement data, the areas and equipment types that should be focused on corrosion problems are proposed.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of the damage of GFRP under 10/350 μs simulated lightning currents
abstract: Glass fiber reinforced polymer (GFRP) was tested to investigate the damage mechanism of wind turbine blade material under lightning currents. The experiments simulate two types of lightning strike discharges, flashover discharge and laminate breakdown discharge. GFRP samples with three different thicknesses were tested under 10/350μs simulated lightning currents. The results show that the damage of the GFRP by lightning strike is mainly thermal decomposition of epoxy resin, the separation, and fracture of glass fiber. In the flashover discharge, the thickness of the samples, the direction of arc and the current amplitude dominates the damage area on the samples.

articleTitle: Review of Lightning Observation on Overhead Distribution Lines in Japan
abstract: The authors summarized observation results related to countermeasures of power distribution lines against lightning strikes. The authors show the observation results of lightning surge due to direct lightning strikes as well as indirect lightning strikes to distribution lines. Moreover damages due to a backflow current from a high structure and a side flash to a distribution line from a tree are shown.

articleTitle: Test and Analysis of Lightning Sensor Based on Lightning Magnetic Field Using a Scale Model
abstract: A series of tests were performed on the lightning sensor based on lightning magnetic field using a scale model with the ratio of 1:10 to the actual wind turbine tower, including waveform test, path test and adjacent lightning test. The results and the analysis show that the lightning sensor can accurately measure the peak value of the lightning current (10/350 μs, 8/20 μs and 2 ms rectangular) with an accuracy of 3%. The current peak value measured by the lightning sensor with the impulse current via the tower wall of the scale model is about 95% of the one measured by the lightning sensor with the same impulse current via the center conductor. At a distance of 2 m from the adjacent lightning discharge (the actual distance is 20 m, according to the model ratio of 1: 10), the lightning sensor is subject to a maximum interference level of 11%.

articleTitle: Modeling of Offshore Wind Turbine Under Lightning Stroke and Analysis of Impact Factors on Transient Overvoltage
abstract: In order to prevent and reduce the offshore wind farm's damage caused by lightning, it's necessary to establish an electromagnetic transient model of the actual discharge flow path, calculate and evaluate the transient overvoltage at the wind turbine's engine room caused by lightning stroke. The accuracy of grounding resistance is an important factor affecting the reliability of the lightning channel model. Considering the wide distribution of China's offshore wind farms and the great difference in sea conditions, the intertidal grounding environment is divided into three layers: seawater layer, silt layer and sandstone layer. The influence of physical depth and resistivity of each layer on grounding resistance is analyzed. Taking the 2MW wind turbine of Shanghai Electric in the intertidal wind farm in Yangkou, Rudong, Jiangsu as an example, the actual discharge flow path is divided into five parts: excitation source, blade, bearing of engine room, tower and grounding resistance. And mathematical models are established respectively. The tower is equivalent to a vertical hollow section cylinder; the bearing between the engine room and the tower is equivalent to the capacitance; the equivalent resistance of each layer is calculated by using the Green function of the soil point current, and the total impact grounding resistance is obtained by superposition. Finally, the whole model is calculated in ATP-EMTP. The relationship between impact factors and the lightning transient effect is analyzed by taking the transient overvoltage at the engine room as an example.

articleTitle: Two Possible Scenarios for the Formation of Category 1 Bipolar Lightning Flashes
abstract: We present and discuss the current and electric field waveforms associated with two upward bipolar lightning flashes that occurred at the Säntis Tower. According to the traditional classification of bipolar flashes, both observed flashes could be classified as Category 1 flashes. The first one belongs to the subcategory la in which the polarity reversal during the initial stage is associated with an in-cloud process, while the second one involves the sequential initiation of two opposite-polarity leaders from the tower.

articleTitle: The Power Loss Calculation Model of Metal Oxide Resistors at Continuous Operating Voltage
abstract: The heat generation of metal oxide resistor due to leakage current flowing through at continuous operating voltage constitutes the internal heat source of surge arrester. The internal heat source directly influences surge arrester stable operating temperature at continuous operating voltage, and affects the ability of surge arrester whether can return to stable operating temperature after absorption of the transient energy. Therefore, in order to obtain the thermal characteristics of surge arrester under transient voltage, the power loss characteristic of resistor in low electric field intensity region should be studied first. A numerical fitting method is proposed for the power loss of resistor in this paper. On the basis of a finite number of measurement points, the calculation expression of power loss variation is fitting with temperature and applied voltage ratio. A model of resistor used in surge arrester of UHV AC transmission system is taking for example. The AC power loss depending on temperature and applied voltage ratio is measured utilizing the resistor power loss measurement system. The fitting method proposed in this paper is implemented to obtain the power loss calculation expression of resistor. The power loss of resistor at different temperature and different applied voltage ratio is calculated. The power loss variation with temperature and applied voltage ratio is analyzed and compared with the measured results. It is shown that the calculation errors are within 12% in the temperature region of 60°C to 150°C, especially higher calculation accuracy about 120°C. The proposed calculation method for fitting power loss expression is valid, and the calculated results can be used in the calculation of surge arrester thermal characteristics as the internal heat source.

articleTitle: The Detailed Time-frequency Analysis of The HF/VHF Emissions Accompanied with CG Lightning Flashes
abstract: In order to obtain the time-frequency domain characteristics of the electromagnetic signal from the whole stages of the Cloud-to-Ground (CG) lightning flashes, including the preliminary breakdown processes, the stepped leaders, the return strokes and the subsequent strokes, we use the lightning signal acquisition platform to collect the electromagnetic signal waveforms concentrated at low frequency(LF), High frequency and Very High frequency (HF/VHF), and carry out the segmentation filtering and the Fourier transform. With the help of Lightning location system (LLS), the time and location of the CG lightning flashes are determined. In this paper, the radiated signal characteristics of CG lightning at different locations and different amplitudes are compared and analyzed. It is concluded that the amplitude of preliminary breakdown processes and return stroke processes is much higher than that of the leaders processes in the frequency range of 30- 350kHz, the preliminary breakdown process, leader and first return stroke of CG lightning have a wide radiation spectrum from 0 to 60MHz, and the subsequent return stroke signal spectra range is relatively concentrated below 10MHz.

articleTitle: Optical signal characteristics of a rocket-triggered lightning at the height of 37.21 m
abstract: An artificial-triggered lightning flash was observed by photodiode at the height of 37.21 m including 17 pulses superposed on the initial continuous current stage, three return strokes and one M-component. The statistical characteristics of initial continuous current pulses, return strokes and M-component were analyzed in this paper. The maximum of peak value of the luminosity in 17 initial continuous current pulses was up to 20.23 digital unit, close to that of the return strokes. Additionally, the scatters for half peak width versus peak value presented the relatively distinguishable trend that along with the peak value increasing, half peak width decreased correspondingly in terms of hyperbolic function. Apart from the light intensity of return strokes, the remaining statistical characteristics of three return stroke like 10-90% risetime, half peak width, front time and tail time were close in value.

articleTitle: Calculating the Potential Difference Between the Ground Electrodes of a Building Struck Directly by Lightning
abstract: We investigated the mechanism by which a lightning strike generates overvoltage at a building's distribution board. We analyzed the overvoltage using VSTL electromagnetic analysis software and constructed a simplified mathematical model for calculating the overvoltage. The results confirmed that the overvoltage generated at the distribution board is not affected by the arrangement of the grounding wires. The overvoltage is instead dominated by the potential difference between the ground electrodes, which is determined by the potential distribution in the surrounding earth. Therefore, the cross-sectional area within the earth through which the lightning current flows out can be modeled using a simple mathematical expression to calculate the potential difference. The overvoltages calculated with the constructed formula coincide with the simulation results within ±10% if the ground electrode is buried within 5 m of the building exterior.

articleTitle: Electric field waveform characteristics of natural cloud-to-ground lightning at different distances
abstract: The electric field measurements of lightning-produced electromagnetic fields are of great importance for lightning location system. In 2014, based on the simultaneously obtained electric fields from multiple sensors of Foshan Total Lightning Location System (FTLLS), 27 natural negative cloud-to-ground (CG) lightning flashes containing 168 electric field waveforms at a distance of 10-86 km in Foshan area were examined in detail. The arithmetic mean (AM) value of initial electric field peak normalized to 100 km for 168 field waveforms is 5.1 V/m. The AM zero-to-peak and 10-90% risetime are 5.6μm and 1.4μm, the AM half-peak width and slow-front duration is 2.5μm and 3.7μm, respectively. The AM zero-crossing time and ratio of peak value to opposite polarity overshoot for 142 waveforms are 31.2μm and 10.5%. The AM second sub-peak amplitudes relative to the initial and the time interval between initial and second peaks are 43.3% and 2.5μm, respectively. In addition, the correlation between electric field waveform characteristics and propagation distance was examined. Some degree of distance dependence for several parameters were also observed.

articleTitle: The Simulation Model and Analysis of Transient Ground Potential Rise of GIS Equipment in Lightning Impact Test
abstract: Gas insulated metal enclosed switchgear and controlgear is a high-voltage electrical equipment widely used in power systems. To ensure the reliability of its operation, GIS equipment needs to be subjected to lightning impulse test at the factory inspection. In the actual lightning impulse test, it is found that if the breakdown occurs during the lightning impulse test, the potential of the casing will increase, and the transient high voltage of the casing will endanger the personal safety of the workers and cause damage to the secondary equipment. In order to study and analyze the whole transient process of equipment after breakdown under lightning impulse, this paper establishes a digital calculation model in ATP-EMTP simulation software,based on the actual GIS test field case, the distribution parameters are used in GIS and GIL simulation calculation, And establish a transient grounding network to calculate the surgical transient ground potential. The analysis results show that the ground potential of the GIS shell is affected by the grounding lead parameters of the equipment, the surface condition, the connection conditions of the GIS equipment and the grounding grid, and the suppression measures of the GIS transient ground potential rise in the lightning impulse test are discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Evaluation Of Lightning Current Parameters Using Measured Lightning Induced Voltage On Distribution Power Lines
abstract: In this paper, an algorithm had been proposed to evaluate the lightning current parameters using measured voltage from overhead distribution lines based on lightning location obtained from lightning location system. Moreover, the performance of algorithm had been considered using different samples of induced voltage. The results showed that the proposed algorithm could determine the lightning current parameters in an acceptable accuracy range. The proposed method is based on the measured values of lightning induced voltage as collecting this parameter is easier and more accessible than electromagnetic field components that had been widely used in past researches.

articleTitle: A Study on the Cable Grounding Condition in Wind Turbines Under Direct Lightning
abstract: Wind turbine is frequently damaged by lightning strikes. Most of damages occur in the control systems. This paper investigates the influence of grounding conditions of the cable sheath on the voltage distribution in control cables. Despite of simplified circuit method in previous WT analysis, this paper adopts a vector fitting enhanced PEEC method to implement a simulation with detailed electromagnetic couplings. Four different grounding conditions are analyzed. It shows that grounding condition has significant influences on the voltage distribution. Grounding at both ends of the WT tower shows the best performance in the view of lightning protection. Meanwhile, the proximity effect among cables will lead to uneven voltage distributions among them. It should be considered when complex cable configuration is used.

articleTitle: Study on Risk Assessment Method of Lightning Disaster about Petroleum in Chongqing
abstract: The product oil tank area and gas station have the characteristics of large quantity, wide distribution, various forms and high risk. At present, there is a lack of an accurate classification standard for the classification of lightning protection categories in such places. Based on GB/T 21714.2-2015, this paper establishes a lightning hazard risk assessment method for Petroleum sites by improving the parameter calculation method of (Risk Assessment Method of Working Conditions, LEC) evaluation method. Thus, a new idea is provided for establishing a unified and clear division criterion, so that lightning protection can be carried out purposefully.

articleTitle: Comparison and Analysis of Lightning Occurrence Characteristics Based on Data Obtained by Fengyun-4A Satellite and ADTD Three-Dimensional Lightning Monitoring Network in Jiangsu Province
abstract: Lightning monitoring data provide foundation for the study of lightning discharge characteristics and activities, which mainly came from two ways: one was satellite monitoring based on optical imaging principle and the other was ground monitoring based on the propagation theory of lightning radiated electromagnetic field. In this study, the characteristics of lightning activities in Jiangsu province during the summer of 2018 (from June to August) were analyzed temporally and spatially, by using the monitoring data of Lightning Mapping Imager(LMI) on Fengyun-4A (FY-4A) satellite which was a new generation of geostationary meteorological satellite launched recently in China and ADTD three-dimensional lightning monitoring network. The results showed that: there were great differences between the two kinds of monitoring data on the variations of seasons and day-to-night ratio, in addition, there was relatively consistence of main peak of daily variation and the spacial intensive area monitored by LMI was further west than monitored by ADTD.

articleTitle: A Quantitative Evaluation Method for Failure Risk of the Lightning Attachment System on Wind Turbine
abstract: The lightning damage seriously affects the normal operation of wind turbines, but there is currently few quantitative analysis methods for the failure risk of the lightning attachment system on wind turbine. Based on leader development model, this paper proposes the definition and calculation method of the lightning shielding failure rate (LSFR) of the lightning attachment system on wind turbine. Taken into the influence of the blade orientation, the LSFR of the blades regarding different lightning attachment systems were comparatively analyzed. The proposed assessment method can provide a theoretical basis for the optimal design and failure risk assessment of the lightning attachment system on wind turbines.

articleTitle: Practical Features of 3D Lightning Mapping System FALMA
abstract: we have examined the accuracy of locating return strokes with Fast Antenna Lightning Mapping Array (FALMA) after excluding CG flashes that may have multiple striking points with different locations. The mean and median errors are 27.4 m and 15.6 m, respectively. Several ground truths collected are basically supportive of such high accuracy of FALMA. It appears that FALMA can be used to assist in locating efficiently the damage mark caused by lightning discharges on various power transmission and distribution equipment. With the data recorded by FALMA during the summer of 2017, which include more 3300 CG flashes, we have performed a simulation on forecasting CG flashes with FALMA at various prediction radiuses and forecast times. With a prediction radius of 10 km and a forecast time of 30 minutes, we found that 99.5% CG flashes can be forecasted. For 98% CG flashes, the prediction lead time is more than 5 minutes. Both the failure prediction and the short lead time deteriorate with the decreasing prediction radius. For different types of applications, the prediction time can be optimized to be as short as several minutes to about 30 minutes.

articleTitle: Study on ac breakdown characteristics of rod - plate gap in sand - dust environment
abstract: In recent years, the influence of dust on the external insulation of power system can not be ignored, but there are not many related researches at home and abroad. In order to study the discharge characteristics under dust environment, this paper selects the rod-plate gap as the research object and builds the dust simulation experiment. The platform is used to conduct experimental research on AC discharge characteristics, and the influence of factors such as gap distance and dust volume fraction on the AC-discharge of the rod-plate gap is obtained. When dust volume fraction is relatively small, AC breakdown voltage of the tip-plate gap decreases with increase of dust volume fraction And the voltage increases with increase of dust volume fraction when sand dust volume fraction is larger. It can be considered that there is a certain dust volume fraction (between 0.5% and 4%), so that the AC gap breakdown voltage is the smallest, and the volume fraction is independent of the gap distance. It can be considered that there is a fixed dust volume fraction (between 0.5% and 4%) that minimizes the gap AC breakdown voltage, which is independent of the gap distance.

articleTitle: Research on Insulation Level and Lightning Protections of 10 kV Overhead Insulated Distribution Lines
abstract: The operation data of the distribution line in the mountainous area indicates that the lightning stroke of the 10kV insulated wire has occurred frequently. Since the insulation level of the distribution line is low, once the phase-to-phase flashover is triggered, the arc root is blocked by the insulation of the line, and it cannot move along the surface of the conductor to cause the wire to fuse at high temperature. This paper analyzes the breaking mechanism of typical 10kV insulated wire, the overvoltage induced by lightning is calculated and the lightning impulse withstand voltage of 10kV insulated wire is obtained through the experiments. On this basis, the lightning protection method of improving the line insulation level by using the combination of insulator and composite insulated crossarm is put forward. At the same time, the addition of silicone rubber insulation sheath on the crossarm surface can significantly improve the pollution flashover insulation level of the line. The impulse insulation level of 80cm length non-sheds composite insulation cross arm can reach 383kV, and the impulse insulation level of 60cm length composite insulated crossarm with sheds can reach 403kV, meeting the lightning protection requirements of 10kV lines in severe pollution areas.

articleTitle: Optical Observations on Propagation Characteristics of Dart Leader in Natural Lightning Striking on Canton Tower
abstract: Based on the high-speed video camera and electric field measurement, dart leader propagation prior to four subsequent return strokes (RS) in one negative lightning flash striking on the top of Canton tower has been recorded. The optical observations show that dart leaders develop downward following the same channel path as the first RS event, with the approximate leader durations ranging from 240 μs to 720 μs and interstroke intervals from 21 ms to 76 ms. Two-dimensional (2D) average speeds of dart leader propagation are mainly in the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> m/s. As the increasing stroke order of the subsequent strokes, the corresponding leader could propagate faster, increasing to the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> m/s, and the luminosity of subsequent stroke could be enhanced. Preceding all the subsequent strokes, there is no clear evidence of upward connecting leaders (UCLs) detected on the top of the tower associated with the descending dart leaders.

articleTitle: Cloud Electrification Model in COSMO Numerical Weather Prediction model
abstract: We developed a Cloud Electrification Model (CEM) and implemented it in the microphysical scheme of the COSMO non-hydrostatic and convection-permitting 2-moment numerical weather prediction model. CEM explicitly describes the electrification of a thundercloud; it explicitly treats the ion motion including the interaction of ions with six kinds of hydrometeors (cloud water, ice, graupel, rain, snow, and hail). Charge concentration within the hydrometeors as well as the change of the concentration are both computed by CEM within the cloud microphysical scheme of COSMO. The charging mechanism in CEM is primarily due to the non-inductive mechanism, which leads to the charge separation and transfer, although we consider the inductive charging mechanism in CEM as well. Based on simulations of an artificially induced thundercloud, i.e. warm air bubble, CEM shows rather complicated electric charge structure in the thundercloud. The concentration of the negative charges is mostly connected to high concentrations of graupel, ice, and snow that frequently collide to transfer their charges.

articleTitle: The Application of Current-Limiting Lightning Rods on High-Rise Buildings
abstract: In recent years, direct lightning strike induced microelectronic device failures have occurred frequently in high-rise buildings across the country. Based on theoretical analysis, this article provides systematic breakdown on the reasons behind the aforementioned incidents from the perspective of direct lightning induced strike backs and electromagnetic fields. In response, a solution pertaining to the application of current-limiting lightning rods is proposed. The effectiveness and necessity of current-limiting lightning rod solutions in high-rise buildings are also illustrated via theoretical analysis and experimental results.

articleTitle: Experimental research on the Effect of Ultraviolet Radiation on 1.5 m air gap discharges
abstract: Comparative research was carried out to explore the effect of ultraviolet radiation on long air gap discharge under positive lightning impulse. U-t characteristic curves were obtained in natural light case and total shading case, separately. The results show that the breakdown voltage increases with ultraviolet radiation, which is contrary to our conjecture. The difference of high speed images and current waves in two cases also demonstrates that ultraviolet radiation does have an effect on the long air gap discharge.

articleTitle: The Application of Multi-Gap Arresters in 10~35kV Overhead Transmission Line
abstract: A multi-gap arresters (MGA) which applied in 10~35kV overhead transmission line is introduced, The feasibility of this product are proved by laboratory investigation and simulation calculation. The product has been applied on several lines in different fields, such as power system, wind farms and oil deposit. Up to date, no lightning tripping accident was reported.

articleTitle: Investigation of an Accelerator Driving Three Microwave Tubes Simultaneously
abstract: A high power accelerator that can simultaneously produce three electron beams is developed. It is made up of primary energy storage system, spiral-strip transformer, pulse forming line using de-ionized water as insulation medium and diode with three cathodes. The three cathodes are stretched into three separate drift tubes, which can isolate the electromagnetic force between the produced electron beams. When a single cathode is connected to the diode, the accelerator can produce over 50 GW electric power and when three cathodes are connected to the diode, three electron beams with over 10 GW electric power are produced. When the accelerator is used to drive three microwave tubes, three microwave of 1 GW (L-band MILO), 1 GW (S-band MILO) and 300 MW (C-band VCO) can be obtained.

articleTitle: A Study on Influence of a Surge Arrester on Multiphase Flashover in Medium-voltage Line
abstract: This paper discusses multiphase flashover in a 6.6kV medium-voltage line in Japan caused by direct lightning strike to the top of a reinforced concrete pole. The multiphase flashover causes a short circuit in the line, and sometimes causes serious damages in power apparatuses and cables. The flashover on an insulator is judged using an integration method, which can consider an influence of voltage waveform on the flashover and can be used in the EMTP. Surge arrester suppresses line voltage and insulator voltage. No flashover occurs on an insulator where a surge arrester is installed on the phase. This paper discusses an influence of a single surge arrester in a non-grounded medium voltage line on multiphase flashover for various combinations of insulator types and the surge arrester.

articleTitle: Research on the Performance of the Lightning Protection System with Overlying Conductors on the Tip of the Wind Turbine Blades
abstract: The wind power system has always focus on the problem of lightning protection of wind turbine blades. Because of the increase of the capacity of wind turbines, the effective height of the wind turbines and the length of the blades also increase a lot, and the problem of the lightning protection failure of the existing blade lightning protection system (LPS) against direct lightning strikes has become prominent as well. There is still short of an optimization design of the LPS which can not only meet engineering requirements but receive all the downward lightning leaders. In this paper, a design scheme of overlying conductors on both of the leading edge and the tailing edge outside the tip of the blade was proposed to solute the delamination damage of the blades. This design of LPS could reduce the vicinal electric field of the down conductors, and reduce the probability of the streamer discharge incept from the down conductor as well as the discharge incept outside the laminate. The experimental study on the lightning protection performance was carried out under lightning and switching impulse voltage. The experimental results showed that the overlying conductors can effectively receive the downward leader to protect the blade from being penetrated in its laying range, but the protection efficiency would decline sharply when the downward leader developed outside the laying range. The covering length of the conductors should be 12% of the total length of the wind turbine blade, which can reduce the lightning damage by 90% or above.

articleTitle: Polarity of Upward Lightning based on Currents Measured at the Gaisberg Tower
abstract: We examined current waveforms of upward flashes initiated from the Gaisberg Tower in 2000 to 2018. Current was measured at the tower-top using a 0.25-mΩ shunt. During this period, 865 flashes were recorded at the Gaisberg Tower, of which 823 (95%) were upward and 4 (0.5%) were downward. For 18 flashes the current waveforms were ambiguous and for 20 flashes they were unsuitable for analysis. Of the 823 upward flashes, 651 (79%) were negative, 35 (4.3%) were positive, and 137 (17%) were bipolar. The median initial stage (IS)-current durations in upward negative, positive, and bipolar flashes were 275, 96, and 282 ms, respectively. The median IS-current peaks in these flashes were 1.4, 3.2, and 1.8 kA, respectively. We expanded the traditional classification of bipolar flashes to include five categories. Of the 137 bipolar flashes, 45% were of Type 1S (single current polarity reversal during IS), 47% of Type 1M (multiple reversals of current polarity during IS), 5.1% of Type 2 (different polarities of current during IS and return stroke), 1.5% of Type 3 (return strokes of different polarities), and 0.73% (one flash) of Type 4 (different polarities of return stroke and the following continuing current).

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration Scheme of Lightning-caused Breakage Prevention Measures for 10kV Distribution Network in Different Landforms
abstract: In recent years, with application of 10kV insulation-covered distribution lines, lightning-caused breakage accidents occur frequently, and reasonable protective measures are urgently needed. The landform has a certain impact on the lightning-caused breakage. Therefore, the lightning activity in Datong area in recent 5 years is analyzed, and the correlation of lightning activity, landform features and distribution network lightning-caused breakage are analyzed. Tests of different protective measures were carried out. The variation law of lightning resistance level and lightning trip-out rate under different lightning protection measures is calculated. The lightning protection effect of lightning protection devices under different installation modes is compared and analyzed. The effect of different protective measures, the landforms and the historical lightning-caused fault are taken into account, and the optimal configuration scheme for improved insulation lines is carried out, which effectively reduces lightning-caused breakage accidents.

articleTitle: LLS Detection for Negative First and Subsequent Return Strokes Measuredat Peissenberg Tower Germany
abstract: In this paper we analyze the currents and electric fields of 5 negative return strokes and compare them with data from the European lightning location system (LLS) EUCLID. The return strokes were measured between May and August 2017 at the Peissenberg Tower, Germany. 1 out of the 5 return strokes was a first return stroke and the remaining 4 were subsequent return strokes. Their peak current Ip varied between 7.5 kA and 24.9 kA, the arithmetic mean value was 14.4 kA. We present high speed video images of the first return stroke showing the extremely long upward connecting leader. The connecting leader produced a continuous current of approximately 30 A. The LLS detected 4 out of the 5 presented return strokes. We present the time errors of the individual sensors, which contributed to the localization. After an optimization process, the time errors were reduced and the location error was minimized. The location error varied between 101 m and 239 m. The peak current inferred by EUCLID was overestimated by 32.3% on average.

articleTitle: Analytical Method for Performance Degradation of Voltage Limiting Type SPD Based on Leakage Current Measurement
abstract: SPD degradation analysis is a key technology of intelligent SPDs. MOV varistor is the core component of voltage limiting type SPD. It is well known that the increase of leakage current is the main factor causing MOV degradation. Therefore, the monitoring of MOV leakage current is the key to judge the operating condition of voltage limiting type SPD. According to the monitored object, it is divided into two categories: the method of full current and the method of resistive current. The full current is simple to implement, since the response sensitivity is low in the initial stage of SPD degradation, which is more common in some low-cost applications; the resistive current measurement method is more complicated to carry out, but can reflect the degradation trend of SPD sensitively and accurately, which is usually applied in some high demand schemes. The measurement methods of resistive current mainly include: active loss, compensation, phase, and harmonic analysis. This paper introduces several methods of leakage current testing, and analyzes the characteristics of various methods. Through a series of experimental data, the measured leakage current data is used to analyze the degradation trend of SPD.

articleTitle: Investigation of altitude dependence of multi-chamber arrester quenching efficiency
abstract: The dependence of multi-chamber arrester quenching efficiency on altitude over sea level was investigated. It was found out that quenching efficiency drops by 20% at pressure of 50 kPa which corresponds to altitude of 5 km.

articleTitle: Lightning fault analysis of 10 kV hybrid distribution lines
abstract: Hybrid structure with electric cables and overhead lines are widely used in the 10 kV urban distribution network. In this paper, simulating conditions of the hybrid network are analyzed as an example, a fault simulation test platform combined of bare conductor, insulated conductor and insulators are established, the failure and the influencing factors are analyzed. The results show that: (1) the insulation damage of insulated conductors is the main reason of the line broken; (2) insulation damage will cause the vicious cycle of equipment insulation, which will causes the insulation damage of cable accessories, and then lead to the fault of the hybrid 10 kV distribution network. Aiming at the fault risk of the hybrid 10 kV distribution network, this paper puts forward some applicable countermeasures. The related research results can provide technical reference for the operation and maintenance of the hybrid 10 kV distribution network.

articleTitle: Potential of GPU-Based Grid Traverse Algorithm for Lightning Geolocation
abstract: Differing from the traditional Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA) lightning location technique, Grid Traverse Algorithm (GTA) is to build up a series of grid points based on numerical discretion of lightning locations in a network region concerned and then to find the lightning location solution by traversing the grid points. Although GTA has advantages over traditional TOA method in many aspects, it is computationally ineffectiveness. To accelerate the GTA processing speed, we have recently proposed a Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) based GTA parallel computing technique, which is proven to be much faster than the existing CPU based GTA technique. In this paper, we give firstly a briefing of the GPU-GTA technique and then the results of performance test of the technique. The performance test is done by applying the GPU-GTA to a specific lightning location network (LLN) with the Monte Carlo simulation approach. The test results show that GPU-GTA can take about 4.3 seconds, 3.6 seconds and 3.2 seconds to locate 1000 points in 3D at the accuracy of 25 m, 50 m and 100 m respectively. The high performance of the GPU-GTA makes it feasible for a real-time LLN with high accuracy.

articleTitle: The Impact of Human Resource Factors on Lightning Safety Performance
abstract: There have been studies in the area of safety guidelines and safety performance in organizational level, but scarce research still exists regarding to the lightning safety performance and its antecedents. This study has identified organizational factors in the area of human resources consist of communication and feedback, incentives and rewards which assume that help to improve lightning safety performance, and examined the degree to which they have contributed to lightning safety performance in Iranian companies. Results confirmed that the factors of communication and feedback, incentives and rewards are positively contributed to lightning safety performance in Iranian manufacturing companies.

articleTitle: Small-Diameter Rogowski Coil and Integrator for Wide-Band Current Sensor
abstract: Current waveforms can effectively be measured using a Rogowski coil. To accurately measure a current waveform, the wide-band frequency characteristics of a current sensor composed of a Rogowski coil and an integration circuit are required. Wide-band current sensors are usually expensive. Therefore, a low-cost and wide-band sensor with high accuracy is needed. The developed wide-band current sensor using a small-diameter Rogowski coil is connected to an oscilloscope, and the current waveform can be measured. The design and manufacturing methods and the evaluation results of the frequency characteristic are introduced in this paper.

articleTitle: Charge-flow and field in soil due to return-stroke
abstract: The evaluation of the electric field gradient along the air-soil interface, generally termed as the step-potential, is an important parameter of practical interest. Generally, the peak value of the step-potential is one of the primary target variables in the design of the earth termination. Two of the most popular approaches used in the literature for its evaluation are the quasi-static approach, in which a lumped current source is employed to inject the return-stroke current to the ground/grounding system and the antenna-model approach, in which a voltage source at the ground end of a monopole is employed to set up the return-stroke current. When viewed in terms of the charge dynamics and in terms of the channel current evolution, both these approaches are found to have certain limitations. This work, by employing a self-consistent return stroke model along with a full representation of the soil, intends to address the above lacunae. It is shown that the step-potential predicted are different for different models and so is the current flow patterns in the soil. Based on the same, the advantage of employing a self-consistent model for the return stroke is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Study on Earth Electrode Matching of Reinforced Concrete Foundation by Simulation Analysis
abstract: The use of the earth electrode of reinforced concrete was examined. By comparing impulse application experiment results and simulation analysis results, the equivalent circuit of reinforced concrete was estimated. Both results agree well, suggesting that reinforced concrete can be used as an earth electrode.

articleTitle: First comparison of measurements of Ka-band cloud radar with lightning in Central Europe
abstract: Situated in Central Europe, the Milešovka observatory was equipped with a vertically oriented Ka-band cloud radar (35 GHz) in spring 2018. We analysed strong convective events that were observed in summer 2018 at the observatory and were detected by the cloud radar, which read high reflectivity values. We applied our algorithm treating the radar data to retrieve vertical air velocity and five types of hydrometeors and we conducted a comparative study of the results with ground-based measurements of lightning. The study showed that hail and rain are the two hydrometeors, which clearly tend to be more frequent in convective clouds that are situated above the cloud radar, when a lightning is recorded in the vicinity of the Milešovka observatory. Similarly, in case of nearby lightning downdrafts are observed at lower altitudes (up to 4 km above the radar), whereas slight updrafts are more typical for higher altitudes above the radar.

articleTitle: Test and Observation of Lightning Shielding Characteristics of ± 1100kV Transmission Lines
abstract: Lightning damage is the one of the main causes of faults in transmission lines. At present, the design of lightning shielding system for ±1100kV UHV DC transmission lines mainly draws on the operating experience of lower voltage transmission lines. Therefore, it is necessary to carry out model tests to study the lightning shielding performance of ±1100kV UHV DC transmission lines. Negative switching impulse of 250/2500μs has been used according to the amplitude and rate of electric field intensity at the surface of the tower. The lightning shielding simulation test is carried out in the plain case with a model ratio of 1:12.5 for the Z38102AL type tower of ±1100kV UHV DC transmission line, and the photography observation with high speed was carried out at the same time. The test results show that the probability curve of the shielding failure spatial region shows an inclined parabola curve, and the lightning shielding failure space of the negative conductor is significantly smaller than that of the positive conductor.
